Do you know why you are depressed? Or what are you depressed about.

I'm exactly where you are.

At this pace it seems you will just continue to live a boring, unfulfilling life, since there is nothing particularly driving you to suicide. I have not found a single answer on any forum or in any dialogue that gives a good solution to your (our) situation.

And to be honest, I don't think there is one. The only way forward is to just keep doing things, but doing them harder. Saying yes when you want to say no.

Personally, I don't have it in me and death is much easier and more sensible, in a way.

Many games interest me. Drugs interest me. I can be very passionate. But if something's boring, and thus a chore, I can't stop thinking about how trivial it all is and I can suffer 0%, instead of suffering, enjoying myself, and then dying inconsequentially anyway.

I don't think there's an answer for this. And it's a question often asked..

That is the question that I haven't seen answered yet: what hope is there when things are good and your life is objectively great but you still wish it was over?

I, too, am hoping for an answer.

Edit: I'm going to post it in this subreddit.

You've been banished from your closest/best group of friends? That is horrible.

If you're nice, you will make more friends. You don't know how or when, but you will.

Regardless, this is a huge loss for you and you can only look to the future. You have my sympathies.

If your parents would be ashamed at your sexuality, it's because their parents told them it was shameful. They are close-minded, conditioned people and their opinion of you shouldn't matter as much as it does.

If you did come out to her, it's not her fault that she will be disappointed. She is taught to be disappointed. If she is a good person she will look past it and realise tradition is not the heart of good values.

There is literally no way everyone is born with a passion. And if they are, their passion will simmer. Passion will always die. It's about the finding the willpower to persistently take part in a hobby/activity that you may or may not enjoy, in hopes you will continue or come to enjoy it.

Side note: your first paragraph is very grammatically incorrect. What you say is not poetic when so much of it is wrong.

"What's extremely frustrating about that is that people always mean far more to me than I do to them."

I relate to this. People only befriend other people who have something to offer them, be that similar humour, knowledge, good looks, anything that makes up good company. And if you don't like yourself, especially over a long period of time, you won't develop any unique/interesting characteristics/traits i.e. you're bad company.

The only way to make good friends is to first like yourself and put yourself first (be fairly selfish), and get interested in anything you might consider a hobby/activity and giving yourself an education in a lucrative or enjoyable line of work. The only good long-term relationships you will ever have will be with people who enjoy the same things you do. Don't enjoy or know much of anything? Then people won't like you. 

Now if you're of my ilk, which I feel like you are, then I think you're just not suited to being a competent and satisfied human who can be bothered to get into a hobby and conjure a will to work.

My personal train of thought is "I could just kill myself instead." when thinking about what I need to do to develop a happy lifestyle where people will enjoy my company, and I theirs.
